title: Vibe CLI + Mistral Devstral 2 — going local
blurb: Why the Vibe CLI asks for an API key, and how to bypass it to run fully local against llama.cpp.
body:
Why an API key is requested: Vibe defaults to Mistral's hosted Devstral 2 model, which requires an account and key. Even if you plan to go local, the CLI initialises by creating a .env or config.toml that expects a MISTRAL_API_KEY entry.

How to bypass / disable the key for local use

  1. Dummy input — if prompted in the terminal, enter any string.
  2. Config edit — open ~/.vibe/config.toml (or ./.vibe/config.toml in your project root).
  3. Local provider settings — point the provider block at a local server with an empty key:

[[providers]] name="llamacpp" · api_base="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1" · api_key_env_var="" · api_style="openai" · backend="generic"

SOURCE · Vibe CLI / Mistral Devstral 2 setup notes.
